description: Bean qou-prjo. Runs the multi-generator (A >= 3) case PR #4848 left open for the transverse NA-Stokes surface-curvature pairing, using the conventions #4848 pinned (Yekutieli ordered partial products; Seifert bands<->crossings; the logarithmic q-derivative germ) in the corpus seminormal/Hoefsmit representation. Canonical multi-nucleon braid words already exist in the corpus (mass_at_3A_proper.atom_braid_word_3A); every atom word, including the A=2 deuteron on 6 strands, is multi-generator, so #4848's single-generator scope-(b) does not reach them. The pairing is nonzero and its 3- and 4-body Moebius cluster residuals are nonzero => SUPER-PAIRWISE. Lean (moebius3_eq_zero, moebius4_eq_zero, sorry-free) proves the pairing is an exactly quadratic cluster functional, so that super-pairwise content is attributable ENTIRELY to context-dependence of the transport, not to a 3-body property of the curvature. The VALUE is NOT determined: the relative residual varies with the germ observer pair, with lambda, and with the nucleon ORDERING -- a genuine many-body binding term cannot depend on nucleon relabelling. Readout is the operator itself (Frobenius norms only size it); ||X||_F^2 = tr(X X^H) is quadratic, so listPairing_trace_zero does not apply, and the scalar trace is reported as a control and vanishes as that theorem requires. Nothing wired, no AME input, free_parameters = 0; the >= 3-body magnitude stays open.

parameters.algebra: H_12(q), seminormal/Hoefsmit; all A=2,3,4 words embed
parameters.germ_convention: logarithmic q-derivative q*(d_q sigma)*sigma^-1, analytic entry derivatives
parameters.transport_convention: Yekutieli ordered partial product along the braid word
parameters.readout: operator (Frobenius norm for size only; quadratic, hence outside listPairing_trace_zero)

caveats: SCOPE-(a). Super-pairwise is a NECESSARY property of the missing >= 3-body term, not a sufficient one; this probe supplies at most one input and does NOT close the binding magnitude. Bean qou-prjo stays OPEN.

The VALUE is gauge-dependent: it varies with the germ observer pair (the corpus pins 'two independent observations' but not which two for n > 3), with lambda, and -- fatally for a many-body observable -- with the nucleon ORDERING. #4798's O(100x) gauge problem is LIVE at A >= 3.

GAUGE CAVEAT ON THE GERM ITSELF: dq = q (d_q rho) rho^-1 transforms like a CONNECTION, not a tensor, under a q-DEPENDENT change of basis (dq -> B dq B^-1 + (1 - Ad(sigma))(q (d_q B) B^-1)). The seminormal basis is q-dependent, so F_q is basis-dependent; #4848 used the reduced-Burau basis and this probe the corpus seminormal basis. The additivity VERDICT is robust across both; the VALUE is not.

Arithmetic: float64 in the sweep (visible cast from the exact mpf word), with an independent mpmath 40-dps re-run of R_3 at dim 11 as the control. The verdict is a 0-vs-O(1e3) question, not a 1-ppQ question. Every numeric field is written as a decimal STRING at binary64's own round-trip width (repr) -- not widened, which would read as precision the numpy sweep never had, and not narrowed, which would stop the witness reproducing.
